title: Riser & Core Critical Quality Check
status: Draft for agreement with James Myers

location.areaHint: e.g. R2, ELV-1, Stair lobby riser

questions.q: Is the riser wall type and fire rating confirmed from the fire strategy (120 min to stair lobby risers, with an E60Sa door)?
Ask the fitter: What is the max distance from the seal to the first service support, and which tested detail is this wall built to? Could they answer?
questions.source: SuperPrime site practice – a fitter who can't answer is a red flag

questions.q: Are floor channel fixings at ≤600 mm centres and head fixings at ≤300 mm, with 2 staggered rows for channels 94 mm and wider?
Is the first fixing no more than 50 mm from the track end, and is the deflection head fitted?
Is the deflection gap to the detail, with no conduit, cable or track inside it?
Are noggins and pattresses to the mark-up, mouse holes closed, and back boxes and conduits in?
Is the riser dry? If the envelope is still open, is FireLine MR or FireCase board being used?

sections.title: OPENINGS: BWIC AND RISER DOOR APERTURES

questions.q: Each BWIC at the drawing size and position (±10 mm), lined for the fire stopper, oversize holes pattressed?
Are there at least 50 mm from the services to the side and bottom of the opening, and at least 150 mm to the soffit at a deflection head?
Is the riser door opening sized to the door schedule within W -0/+10 mm and H -0/+5 mm?
Is there at least 200 mm of standard wall either side of and above the riser door frame, at least 300 mm between adjacent apertures, and an upstand of at least 100 mm?
Is a timber insert fitted on all 4 sides of the opening in a steel stud wall, unless Selo has confirmed it isn't needed for this shaft wall?
Dry riser cabinet opening the box size plus fixing tolerance (box fits without forcing)?

sections.title: MEP 1st FIX: ALL SERVICES THROUGH OPENINGS

questions.q: Is the first support within 400 mm of the seal, or within 300 mm each side for Argus sprinkler pipe?
Are like services at least 50 mm apart, uninsulated metal pipes at least 100 mm apart, and the spacing within the tested detail?
Are services independently supported so no load sits on the seal?
Equipment in its drawn position; tray/ladder fixed; containment not over-filled?
SWAs cleated, dressed, bend radius at least 6–8× cable diameter, metal ties?
questions.source: BS 7671 cable bend radius; Borough riser checklist

questions.q: Earth bonding complete, cable ends labelled, danger notices fitted, 600 mm access kept in front of equipment?
Is copex taken to the top of containment, with edge trim and unistrut end caps fitted?
Has the pipework been pressure tested before insulation?
Can isolation valves still be operated once lagged, are drain cocks accessible and not buried, and is the insulation undamaged?
Are pipework IDs and flow direction labelled, and the riser clean?
Are vertical duct bearers Type A or B (RSA/RSC to span table) on fire-rated anchors?
Is each smoke or fire damper supported at every corner, fire stopped to the Mandik tested detail, with its actuator cover removable?
Has DW/143 leakage testing been done in all risers, and have the dampers been drop-tested?
Is the pipe 100 mm galvanised, with long-radius bends and brackets to the table (at least 1 within 1 m of each mechanical joint)?
Is the lowest point of the landing valve at least 750 mm above FFL, with "DRY RISER OUTLET" labelling and the pipe equipotentially bonded?
Is the air release valve above the highest landing valve, and are the isolation valves chained and padlocked open?
Has the test been done (air at 0.5 bar for 15 min, then water at 12 bar for 10 min), witnessed by MPX, with a permit to fill?
Outlet in its final orientation, cabinet glass intact, surround made good?
Are fire alarm cables on their own supports, using metal clips?
Are cables tested before covering or fire stopping?
Is the opening ready for fire stopping (services complete, supported, gaps right)?
CLM operative on site has their FIRAS card, and the fire rating label matches the wall?
Does the fire stopping match the benchmark, with the seal label fitted?
Where the riser meets a floating floor or the top of a void, is the void fire stopped?
Is every penetration in an AV or ELV riser sealed, with no unsealed re-entry?
Has the MEP handover been received (HP), sockets and draw wires and putty pads fitted, and photos taken before closure?
Board screws at 300 mm (200 mm at corners), joints staggered 600 mm, mouse holes closed, wall ±3 mm in 1.8 m?

guide.title: Drylining – British Gypsum figures
rows: 600 mm max (400 mm where specified / tiled)
max 50 mm from the track end
studs NOT screwed to the head track; 15–20 mm gap kept
guide.note: SJWS Field issues: studs screwed to the head track, corner screws at 290 mm, stagger only 123 mm – all fails.
guide.src: British Gypsum White Book (Gypwall / GypLyner) – confirm wall type; MEA ITP acceptance criteria; Field issues

questions.q: Is fire tape complete and the smoke seal taped and jointed?
Is the door frame fixed solid, with the door label/plug in place and undamaged?
Are frame gaps filled with intumescent acrylic and sealant joints formed?
Is the threshold level and square to the frame and leaf, with voids sealed?
Are smoke and acoustic seals fitted? Doors are Rw 35 dB for mechanical and public health, and Rw 30 dB for electrical.
Is the door label present (manufacturer, rating, serial), the FDKS sign fitted, and the lock and ironmongery to schedule?
Was the door fitted after wet trades had dried (no swelling or water marks)?
Is the grating GRP, cut to ±5 mm, clipped, with no rocking?
Are cut-outs around services neat, with no clash with supports or the ladder?
Is the roof riser opening weatherproofed, and the riser dry with no staining?
Are all services labelled: cables, pipes, ducts, dampers, dry riser and seals?
Is riser lighting working?
questions.source: Not found in the ITPs or tech subs. Confirm against the Borough spec

questions.q: Is the ladder or access in place, and are valves, dampers and isolators reachable?
Is the riser clean, with no swarf, offcuts or redundant rods, and all rods capped?

activity: Riser shaft walls, openings, services, fire stopping, doors
itp: MEA, CLM, PBS, Borough, Argus, PHF, GCL ITPs

notOk.t: Service supports more than 400 mm from the fire-stopped shaft wall / slab (tested detail)
Fire seal missing between board and concrete inside the riser
Conduit or cables run through the shaft wall instead of a sealed penetration
Wrong channel cloaking I-studs at shaftwall ends (60SC55 on 60 mm I-studs distorts the wall)
Riser at floating floor / void top not fire stopped
Cables loose or on plastic ties only – metal ties and copex at containment ends
Unistrut and stud end caps missing
Riser not cleaned out, water damage to drylining left in place

ask.q: What's the riser wall type and rating?
ask.a: From the fire strategy – they can name it (e.g. 120 min to the stair lobby).

ask.q: What gap from services to the opening edges?
ask.a: At least 50 mm to the side and bottom, and the CLM matrix gaps between services.

ask.q: What size tolerance on the riser door opening?
Who fire stops the BWIC openings and when?
ask.a: CLM, after services are in and before close-up – logged.
